narrative.overview:
The Staff app is the category standard for a working tool, executed at the craft level of Linear, Stripe Dashboard and GOV.UK services (PRODUCT.md, Brand Commitments, chosen 2026-11-08). A doula or an owner opening Clients should know where everything is before noticing the look: a top bar with the nav, a title with one start action beside it, a filter bar, a result line, a table. Nothing about the arrangement is novel. The character is that nothing is out of place: every row is the same height, every number lines up, every badge means one thing, and both themes are proved, not hoped for.

The working ground is near-white in light and a deep blue-gray in dark (the 3am scene), with a near-black ink, neutral hairlines, and one blue spent on links, the primary action and the marker of where you are. Hanken Grotesk runs at a small, strict scale whose floor is 16px everywhere. Density is a desk tool's: a 40px table row at a fine pointer, 44px wherever an input can tap. The two worlds this one refuses are the costume world (a themed skin that performs a mood) and the half-finished default (a gray screen, one accent, loose spacing).

The Staff app has no signature component yet. The candidate, the care timeline (each Client's care as a block on a time axis), is not built; it is under test and is kept only if it beats a plain Due column on the Clients rubric's jobs. Until one wins, distinctiveness comes from craft alone.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white working ground, near-black ink, neutral hairlines; nothing pure white or pure black in either theme.
One blue, for links, the primary action, the current place and the focus ring.
Quiet filled badges, one meaning per hue app-wide.
Hanken Grotesk, one 1.25 ratio from a 16px floor, fluid on the container, never under 16px.
Tabular figures on every date, amount and count in a table.
Flat surfaces; depth is a tonal ladder and a hairline, never a shadow.
One corner radius (8px), plus the pill for badges.
Layout answers the space it is given (container queries), from 320px up.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: The primary is spent on links, the primary action or start link, the marker of the current place (nav item, step, applied chip), the focus ring and the selection tint. A decorative icon or a progress track is Secondary Ink, not blue. A start link and a primary Button never share a screen region: the accent is spent once.

rules.name: The One Meaning Per Hue Rule
rules.body: Amber is owes or a warning, red is overdue or an error, blue is information or pending, green is success, gray is neutral, app-wide. A new state picks the meaning it shares, never a new hue. `Badge.svelte.spec.ts` holds the five tints visibly apart and their text at 4.5:1 in both themes; `clients-list.svelte.spec.ts` holds a pending Request to the blue badge so amber stays for what a Client owes.

rules.name: The Derived Dark Rule
rules.body: The dark theme is derived, not invented: hues are held, only lightness moves, and the surface ladder inverts so the page ground is the darkest step. The system-preference block and the `[data-theme]` override are byte-identical, and `tokens.spec.ts` proves both, and the shell palette, against the WCAG floors.

rules.name: The Night Walls Rule
rules.body: The Staff top bar and its narrow menu sheet carry `data-shell`, inside which every color token resolves to one night palette in both themes: night-blue walls over a pale work area by day, a step deeper than the page at night. Components inside the bar read the same tokens they read anywhere.

rules.name: The Themed Browser Rule
rules.body: The browser's own surfaces follow the theme: `color-scheme` is declared in every theme block, the root canvas is the page ground, the selection is a 28% primary tint with ink text, the caret is ink, the scrollbar is thin in the Control Edge color, and the favicon and manifest take their colors from the tokens (`tokens.usage.spec.ts` holds the favicon). Selection, caret and scrollbar are build-held in `base.css`, not yet spec-held.

rules.name: The One Title Rule
rules.body: Every page title is the page Heading at `heading-lg`. `templates/pageTitle.usage.spec.ts` fails a raw `<h1>` outside QuestionPage, a title at another step, or a level-1 Heading in another variant; `expectOneFramedHeading` holds one `<h1>` per screen inside the Template's frame.

rules.name: The Sixteen Floor Rule
rules.body: No text is under 16px at any width (ADR-0060). Hierarchy below the headings is weight, leading, tracking and ink, never a smaller size.

rules.name: The Lined-Up Figures Rule
rules.body: Every date, amount and count is set in tabular figures. DataTable sets it on every cell and right-aligns a numeric column, header and body alike (`DataTable.svelte.spec.ts`); `base.css` also sets it on `time`, `data`, `output`, `dd` and `.tabular` (build-held).

rules.name: The No Shouting Rule
rules.body: No text is set in all caps; size, weight and tracking already make the hierarchy (`tokens.usage.spec.ts`). A component sets no font size, weight or tracking outside the scale.

rules.name: The Named Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Space is chosen by what it separates: `--space-label` (step 1) a label from its own hint and control; `--space-related` (step 3) items that read as one group; `--space-field` (step 5) one field from the next; `--space-group` (step 7) a group, or the page title, from the next; `--space-section` (step 8) one section from the next.

rules.name: The One Left Edge Rule
rules.body: A screen's regions share the Template frame's inline-start edge; nothing is indented off it or centered away from it. Build-held through the Templates; the framed-title check is the only part a spec measures today.

rules.name: The Desk Density Rule
rules.body: A table row is 40px with a fine pointer and 44px of target plus its 1px rule when any input can tap (`--row-height`); a link or Button in a row takes the row's height as its floor, so the row never grows. Every standalone target is at least 44px in both directions (`--hit-target-min`). Inline links inside a sentence are excepted.

rules.name: The Tone Not Shadow Rule
rules.body: A surface separates from the one under it by a step on the surface ladder or a hairline. Nothing floats.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: 8px or a full pill. A card is never rounder than a Button.

dos: **Do** spend the primary only on a link, the primary action or start link, the current place, the focus ring and the selection tint.
**Do** pick a status hue by meaning: amber owes or warning, red overdue or error, blue information or pending, green success, gray neutral.
**Do** set every date, amount and count in tabular figures, and right-align a numeric column.
**Do** draw every page title as the page Heading at `heading-lg`, inside the Template's frame, on the frame's left edge.
**Do** separate surfaces by a step on the surface ladder or a hairline.
**Do** answer the container with a container query, and check every screen at 320px and in both themes.
**Do** read spacing by its named rhythm (`--space-label`, `--space-related`, `--space-field`, `--space-group`, `--space-section`).
donts: **Don't** use pure white or pure black, in either theme.
**Don't** name a color, a px length or a font size of a component's own; spend a token (`tokens.usage.spec.ts`).
**Don't** set text in all caps or under 16px.
**Don't** add a second corner radius or a cast shadow.
**Don't** give a new state a new hue, or use amber for anything but owes or a warning.
**Don't** use a width media query or a static `vw` for layout.
**Don't** put a start link beside a primary Button.
